file: 2020-02-05_Baillargeon_v_Kings_County_Waterproofing_Corp_4724525.txt
case_name: Baillargeon v Kings County Waterproofing Corp.
reason: The jury verdict was not contrary to the weight of the evidence because it was based on a fair interpretation of the evidence.

file: 2022-08-24_Rider_v_Manhattan_Monster_Inc_7859429.txt
case_name: Rider v Manhattan Monster, Inc.
reason: The defendant established the decorative throne was open and obvious and not inherently dangerous, and the plaintiff failed to raise a triable issue of fact.

file: 2025-09-24_Coates_v_Brooklyn_Hosp_Ctr_10677055.txt
case_name: Coates v Brooklyn Hosp. Ctr.
reason: The plaintiff was unable to identify the location or cause of her fall without engaging in speculation, and her opposition affidavit merely raised a feigned issue of fact.

file: Alvarez v Staten Is. R.T. Operating Auth. (2024 NY Slip Op 01695).txt
case_name: Alvarez v Staten Is. R.T. Operating Auth.
reason: The plaintiff could not identify the cause of her fall without engaging in speculation, which is fatal to a negligence claim.

file: Binger Mei v. Kim Wan Cheung.txt
case_name: Binger Mei v Kim Wan Cheung
reason: The court affirmed because the plaintiff established the driver's negligence and proximate cause through deposition testimony, while the driver's contention that the pedestrian crossed outside the crosswalk was speculative and raised no triable issue of fact.

file: Blake v. New York City Tr. Auth..txt
case_name: Blake v New York City Tr. Auth.
reason: The appellate court affirmed the lower court’s denial of summary judgment because the transit defendants failed to prove they were not negligent under the emergency doctrine and could not establish an emergency caused by their own actions, leaving material factual disputes unresolved.

file: Cangelosi v. New York City Tr. Auth..txt
case_name: Cangelosi v New York City Transit Authority
reason: Defendants established the emergency doctrine by demonstrating the bus driver's sudden stop was precipitated by a pedestrian running in front, and the plaintiff failed to raise a triable issue of negligence.

file: Carranza v. Memorial Hosp. for Cancer & Allied Diseases.txt
case_name: Carranza v Memorial Hosp. for Cancer & Allied Diseases
reason: The court granted plaintiff summary judgment on Labor Law § 240(1) because the falling object should have been secured by a safety device, but affirmed dismissal of Labor Law § 200 and negligence claims against the general contractor because the accident arose from the means and methods of work controlled by plaintiff's employer.

file: Choudhary v. DiSilvio.txt
case_name: Choudhary v DiSilvio
reason: The court held that genuine issues of fact existed about fault, so summary judgment was properly denied.

file: Correa v. Cannon.txt
case_name: Correa v Cannon
reason: The defendant driver's affidavit raised triable issues of fact as to whether the plaintiff driver made a sudden stop for no apparent reason, providing a nonnegligent explanation for the rear-end collision.

file: Cromer-Walker v. Singh.txt
case_name: Cromer-Walker v Singh
reason: The plaintiff established a prima facie case of liability by showing he was in a crosswalk with the signal in his favor when struck, and the defendants failed to present evidence to create a triable issue of fact.

file: E.B. v. Gonzalez.txt
case_name: E.B. v Gonzalez
reason: The plaintiffs established prima facie entitlement to summary judgment on liability by showing the infant plaintiff was lawfully in a crosswalk with an active pedestrian signal when struck, and the defendant driver's admission of being blinded by foreseeable sun glare did not constitute a qualifying emergency or raise a triable issue of fact.

file: Edwards v Genting N.Y., LLC (2023 NY Slip Op 03223).txt
case_name: Edwards v Genting N.Y., LLC
reason: Defendant failed to establish prima facie lack of constructive notice of the ice condition, providing no evidence of prior inspection and leaving triable issues of fact regarding the condition's duration.

file: Fischetti v. Simonovsky.txt
case_name: Fischetti v Simonovsky
reason: The court granted summary judgment on liability because the defendant could not provide a nonnegligent explanation for the rear‑end collision, but denied dismissal of the comparative negligence defense because the plaintiff’s affidavit did not sufficiently show she was free of fault.

file: Gaston v. Vertsberger.txt
case_name: Gaston v Vertsberger
reason: The plaintiff's affidavit demonstrated he was walking within a crosswalk with the pedestrian signal in his favor when the defendant's vehicle failed to yield the right-of-way, establishing a prima entitlement to judgment as a matter of law, and the defendant failed to raise a triable issue of fact.

file: Harrington v New York City Tr. Auth. (2024 NY Slip Op 00296).txt
case_name: Harrington v New York City Transit Authority
reason: The court held that the fare box's condition was not a proximate cause of the plaintiff's slip and fall, rendering the requested discovery immaterial and unnecessary.

file: Holton v. New York City Tr. Auth..txt
case_name: Holton v New York City Tr. Auth.
reason: The plaintiff established her prima facie case of negligence through deposition testimony showing the defendant rear-ended a stopped vehicle, and the defendant failed to provide a nonnegligent explanation for the collision.

file: Hyland v. MFM Contr. Corp..txt
case_name: Hyland v MFM Contr. Corp.
reason: The court found triable issues of fact regarding whether the construction fence created a foreseeable unreasonable risk to pedestrians and whether the plaintiff's conduct was a superseding cause, so summary judgment for MFM and Tectonic was denied while the City's was affirmed.

file: Leem v 152-24 N., LLC (2022 NY Slip Op 00417).txt
case_name: Leem v 152-24 N., LLC
reason: The court affirmed the denial of summary judgment because the deposition testimony raised a triable issue as to whether the plaintiff tripped on the mat covering the sloped sidewalk, and the defendant failed to make a prima facie showing that it did not create or have notice of the hazardous condition.

file: Merchant v New York City Tr. Auth. (2020 NY Slip Op 02666).txt
case_name: Merchant v New York City Tr. Auth.
reason: The court reversed because the transit authority failed to make a prima facie showing that it lacked constructive notice of the wet floor by offering no evidence of when the area was last cleaned or inspected.

file: Neary v. New York City Tr. Auth..txt
case_name: Neary v New York City Tr. Auth.
reason: The court reversed the denial of summary judgment because the transit authority established the emergency doctrine and plaintiff failed to raise a triable issue of fact regarding negligence.

file: O'Connor v. Tishman Constr. Corp..txt
case_name: O'Connor v Tishman Constr. Corp.
reason: The Court reversed the summary judgment dismissals because conflicting evidence created triable issues as to the City's responsibility for the sidewalk defect, the Tishman defendants failed to establish they did not cause it, and the adjacent property owners had a nondelegable duty to maintain the sidewalk safely.

file: Pascall v. New York City Tr. Auth..txt
case_name: Pascall v New York City Tr. Auth.
reason: The court affirmed the denial of the MTA defendants’ motion to dismiss because the plaintiff’s allegations plausibly stated a respondeat superior claim arising from the MTA defendants’ alleged control over the vehicle operator.

file: Powell v. City of New York.txt
case_name: Powell v City of New York
reason: The court reversed because the City failed to make a prima facie showing of the absence of a Labor Law nexus and the permit-related testimony was speculative, leaving triable issues of fact.

file: Rivera v. City of New York.txt
case_name: Rivera v City of New York
reason: The court affirmed summary judgment for the defendants because the plaintiff failed to raise a triable issue of fact establishing defendants’ responsibility for the alleged uneven roadway.

file: Tejada-Rodriguez v. 76 Eleventh Ave. Prop. Owner LLC..txt
case_name: Tejada-Rodriguez v 76 Eleventh Ave. Prop. Owner LLC.
reason: The court affirmed partial summary judgment because Omnibuild was the plaintiff's employer or statutory agent under Labor Law § 240(1), exercised sufficient control over the work, and the defendants failed to raise a material factual dispute.

file: Warshak v. City of New York.txt
case_name: Warshak v City of New York
reason: The court affirmed summary judgment because the City established a safe roadway condition and lacked actual notice of the hazard, while the plaintiff failed to raise a triable issue through an unsupported expert opinion or an unauthenticated photograph.

file: Weiss v Bay Club (2022 NY Slip Op 03026).txt
case_name: Weiss v Bay Club
reason: The court reversed because the defendants failed to make a prima facie showing that the plaintiff could not identify the cause of her fall or that they lacked constructive notice of the defective step.

file: Yearwood v. New York City Tr. Auth..txt
case_name: Yearwood v New York City Tr. Auth.
reason: The court reversed because the defendants’ affidavit and surveillance video raised triable issues as to negligence and the emergency doctrine, defeating the plaintiff’s motion for summary judgment and dismissal of that defense.

file: Shuttleworth v Saint Margaret's R.C. Church in Middle Vil. (2022 NY Slip Op 05730).txt
case_name: Shuttleworth v Saint Margaret's R.C. Church in Middle Vil.
reason: The court reversed and granted summary judgment to the defendant because the wet drainage grate was not shown to be defective or hazardous, and the plaintiff failed to raise a triable issue of fact.

file: McGahan v Brooklyn Pub. Lib. (2022 NY Slip Op 05846) .txt
case_name: McGahan v Brooklyn Pub. Lib.
reason: The Court affirmed summary judgment because the Library established that it neither created the hazardous condition nor had actual or constructive notice of it, and the plaintiff failed to raise a triable issue as to how long the condition existed.
